subtitle: Understand how bass note choice affects harmonic stability and melodic bass lines

backLink.label: Back to Chord Theory in Songs

introduction.title: The Power of the Bass Note
introduction.text: A chord inversion is simply putting a different chord tone in the bass. This small change dramatically affects the chord's stability, function, and how it connects to other chords. It's the difference between choppy chord changes and smooth, professional-sounding progressions.

columns.title: Voice Leading
columns.text: Inversions create smooth bass lines and better voice leading between chords

columns.title: Stability Control
columns.text: Choose stability levels: root position = stable, inversions = less stable

columns.title: Melodic Bass
columns.text: Turn your bass line into a melody that supports the harmony

sections.title: When and Why to Use Inversions

fields.label: Problem
fields.value: Chord changes sound choppy or disconnected

fields.label: Solution
fields.value: Use inversions to create stepwise bass motion

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C - F becomes C - F/A (bass moves C-A instead of C-F)

fields.label: Problem
fields.value: Bass line lacks interest or direction

fields.label: Solution
fields.value: Choose inversions to create singable bass melodies

fields.label: Example
fields.value: I - vi - IV - V becomes I - vi/I - IV - V/VII

fields.label: Solution
fields.value: Use root position for strong beats, inversions for weak

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Strong beat = root position, passing beat = inversion

fields.label: Problem
fields.value: Chord voicings don't fit the style

fields.label: Solution
fields.value: Match inversion usage to genre expectations

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Folk: more inversions, Rock: more root position

cards.title: Paul McCartney's Masterful Use of Inversions

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: I - V/VII - vi - IV (with G/B inversion)

items: The G/B (first inversion) creates a beautiful descending bass line C-B-A-F
Creates melodic bass line that supports the vocal
G/B is less stable than G, keeps motion flowing
Descending line mirrors emotional content
Smooth voice leading throughout
Alternative: C - G - Am - F would have bass line C-G-A-F (awkward leap)

cards.title: Piano

fields.label: Practice Techniques
fields.value: Practice inversions across the entire keyboard; Use left hand for bass note, right for upper structure; Learn common voicing patterns; Practice scales using different inversion patterns

items: Spread voicings across both hands for rich sound
Use pedal to connect inverted chords smoothly
Practice "walking" bass lines with right hand chords

cards.title: Guitar

fields.label: Practice Techniques
fields.value: Learn moveable inversion shapes up the neck; Practice bass note on lowest available string; Use partial chords; Combine open strings with fretted inversions

items: Focus on clarity - not all notes need to sound
Use thumb for bass notes when necessary
Learn which chord tones are most important

cards.title: Bass Guitar

fields.label: Practice Techniques
fields.value: Think about the harmonic function of your note choice; Use chord tones other than root for sophistication; Practice walking bass lines using inversions; Coordinate with other instruments' voicings

items: Root position for stability, inversions for movement
Use inversions to outline chord progressions
Consider the melody when choosing bass notes
